t: Text generation — which models write best
title: Text generation — which models write best
description: Text generation is the core capability: producing fluent, coherent prose from a prompt — stories, emails, articles, dialogue. Nearly every large language model does it, but they differ in voice control, instruction fidelity, and cost. The models below are the ones teams actually reach for when the job is 'write well.'

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4
models.note: Excellent long-form prose and tone matching

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.note: Great with very long briefs (1M context)

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.note: Best open-weight option for self-hosted writing

best_pick: Claude Sonnet 4 for quality prose; Llama 3.3 70B when it must be self-hosted.
example_use: Drafting a product launch email in a specific brand voice.

demo.notes: Chooser pattern; wire the pick to any provider SDK.

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Reasoning & problem solving — models that think
title: Reasoning & problem solving — models that think
description: Reasoning models spend extra compute on an internal chain of thought before answering, which makes them dramatically better at math, logic puzzles, science, and multi-step planning. This is a distinct capability from fluent chat: a model can write beautifully and still fail arithmetic. When the task is hard thinking, pick from this list.

models.name: o3
models.note: Adjustable reasoning effort; top STEM scores

best_pick: o3 (high effort) for max accuracy; DeepSeek-R1 for open/cheap reasoning.
example_use: Solving a competition math problem with verifiable steps.

demo.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
# reasoning capability: ask for effort, get a trace-backed answer
r = client.chat.completions.create(model="o3", reasoning_effort="high",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "How many trailing zeros does 100! have? Show reasoning."}])
print(r.choices[0].message.content)

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Code generation — models that program
title: Code generation — models that program
description: Code generation means producing working programs from natural-language specs — functions, scripts, full modules, tests. The best code models are trained heavily on repositories, understand many languages, and increasingly work with whole-repo context. Fill-in-the-middle support matters for IDE completion.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4
models.note: Leads public benchmarks on real coding tasks

models.name: Codestral 22B
models.note: Open code specialist, 80+ languages, FIM support

models.name: GPT-4o
models.note: Strong generalist coder with tool use

models.name: Qwen2.5-Coder 32B
models.note: Top open coder in its size class

best_pick: Claude Sonnet 4 for agentic coding; Codestral for self-hosted completion.
example_use: Generating a tested Python module from a spec.

demo.code:
# Self-hosted code completion with an open code model:
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct")
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct", device_map="auto")
ids = tok("def quicksort(arr):", return_tensors="pt").input_ids
print(tok.decode(model.generate(ids, max_new_tokens=120)[0]))
demo.notes: Real transformers pattern for an open code model.

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Long-context document analysis — models that read everything
title: Long-context document analysis — models that read everything
description: Some tasks require holding an entire corpus in mind at once: a 500-page contract set, a full codebase, a season of transcripts. Long-context models (200K–1M+ tokens) do in one prompt what used to need chunking pipelines. The capability to watch for is not just window size but retrieval accuracy deep inside the window.
best_pick: Gemini 2.5 Pro when it must all fit at once.
example_use: Answering questions across a 300-page technical manual.

demo.code:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(api_key="YOUR_KEY")
manual = open("manual.txt").read()  # up to ~750k words fits
resp = client.models.generate_content(model="gemini-2.5-pro",
    contents=["List every safety warning in this manual:", manual])
print(resp.text)

t: Translation — models across languages
title: Translation — models across languages
description: Machine translation ranges from dedicated encoder-decoder models (best for low-resource languages) to giant LLMs (best for nuance, tone, and formatting). For document translation with layout preserved, LLM-based approaches now win; for raw coverage of 200 languages, specialized models still lead.

models.name: NLLB-200
models.note: Open model covering 200 languages, low-resource strong

best_pick: NLLB-200 for breadth; GPT-4o/Claude for nuance.
example_use: Translating a product manual into 12 languages with consistent terminology.

demo.code:
from transformers import pipeline
pipe = pipeline("translation", model="facebook/nllb-200-distilled-600M",
                  src_lang="eng_Latn", tgt_lang="swh_Latn")
print(pipe("Knowledge belongs to everyone.")[0]["translation_text"])

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Summarization — models that compress
title: Summarization — models that compress
description: Summarization compresses long inputs into faithful short outputs — meeting notes, papers, threads. The failure mode is hallucinated details, so the best summarizers are models with strong grounding: they stick to the source. Length control (one sentence vs. one page) is the key prompting skill.

models.name: BART-large-CNN
models.note: Classic open summarizer, cheap at scale

best_pick: Claude Sonnet 4 for faithful abstracts; BART for bulk/cheap.
example_use: Daily digest of 50 support tickets.

demo.code:
from transformers import pipeline
pipe = pipeline("summarization", model="facebook/bart-large-cnn")
text = open("tickets.txt").read()
print(pipe(text, max_length=120, min_length=40)[0]["summary_text"])

t: Math solving — models that calculate
title: Math solving — models that calculate
description: Math capability splits three ways: reasoning models that work problems step-by-step, specialized math models trained on formal problem sets, and tool-using models that offload arithmetic to code execution. For contest-level problems, reasoning models lead; for verified computation, code execution wins.

models.name: o3
models.note: Top reasoning scores on math benchmarks

models.name: DeepSeek-R1
models.note: Open reasoning, strong on competition math

best_pick: o3 for proof-style; code execution for verified numbers.
example_use: Solving and checking a calculus problem set.

demo.code:
# Verified math: let the model write code, then RUN it
import sympy as sp
x = sp.symbols("x")
print(sp.integrate(x**2 * sp.exp(x), x))  # model-generated, machine-checked
# Pair any LLM above with a Python tool for trustworthy math
demo.notes: Pattern: LLM writes SymPy, Python executes — no arithmetic hallucinations.

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Image understanding — models that see
title: Image understanding — models that see
description: Vision-language models answer questions about images: what's in this photo, read this chart, what's wrong with this UI screenshot. The leaders combine strong language reasoning with high-resolution image encoders; open models have closed much of the gap for document and chart reading.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.note: Excellent on charts, video frames, long visual docs

best_pick: Gemini 2.5 Pro for dense visuals; Qwen2.5-VL when it must be open.
example_use: Extracting data from a photographed chart.

demo.code:
from openai import OpenAI
client = OpenAI()
r = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o", messages=[{"role": "user", "content": [
    {"type": "text", "text": "Read the values off this bar chart as JSON."},
    {"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": "https://example.com/chart.png"}}]}])
print(r.choices[0].message.content)

t: Image generation — models that draw
title: Image generation — models that draw
description: Text-to-image models render pictures from descriptions. They differ on photorealism vs. stylization, prompt adherence, text rendering inside images, and whether you can self-host. The open ecosystem (Stable Diffusion family, FLUX) dominates customization via fine-tunes.
best_pick: DALL-E 3 for ease; FLUX.1/SD3.5 for self-hosted control.
example_use: Generating product mockups from text briefs.

demo.code:
from diffusers import FluxPipeline
import torch
pipe = FluxPipeline.from_pretrained("black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-dev", torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16).to("cuda")
img = pipe("a ceramic vase, studio lighting, product photo", num_inference_steps=28).images[0]
img.save("vase.png")

t: Video generation — models that film
title: Video generation — models that film
description: Text-to-video models synthesize short clips from prompts (optionally from a starting image). The frontier is Veo 3's native audio and Sora's coherence; the practical axis is clip length, consistency of characters across shots, and cost per second.
best_pick: Veo 3 when sound matters; Sora for visual coherence.
example_use: A 10-second product ad from one prompt.

demo.code:
from google import genai
client = genai.Client(api_key="YOUR_KEY")
op = client.models.generate_videos(model="veo-3.0-generate-001",
    prompt="Product shot: headphones rotating on a pedestal, studio light")
while not op.done:
    op = client.operations.get(op)
print("done")
demo.notes: Real Veo pattern; download the file from op.response.

t: OCR & document understanding — models that read paperwork
title: OCR & document understanding — models that read paperwork
description: Reading documents means more than characters: layout, tables, handwriting, and meaning. Classical OCR (Tesseract, PaddleOCR) is fast and free; vision-language models now read messy scans and reason over tables better than any OCR pipeline alone. The winning stack is often both: OCR for speed, VLM for understanding.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.note: Reads messy scans + reasons over tables

best_pick: PaddleOCR for bulk; a VLM for understanding.
example_use: Digitizing a filing cabinet of invoices.

demo.code:
from paddleocr import PaddleOCR
ocr = PaddleOCR(lang="en")
for line in ocr.ocr("invoice.png")[0]:
    print(line[1][0], line[1][1])  # text, confidence

t: Object detection — models that find things in pictures
title: Object detection — models that find things in pictures
description: Object detection draws boxes around things in images — people, products, defects. YOLO-family models are the real-time standard; open-vocabulary detectors like Grounding DINO find arbitrary objects from text descriptions without retraining.
best_pick: YOLOv11 for speed; Grounding DINO for open vocabulary.
example_use: Counting products on store shelves from photos.

demo.code:
from ultralytics import YOLO
model = YOLO("yolo11n.pt")
for r in model("shelf.jpg"):
    print(r.boxes.cls.tolist(), r.boxes.xyxy.tolist())

t: Speech recognition — models that transcribe
title: Speech recognition — models that transcribe
description: Speech-to-text converts audio to words, increasingly with timestamps, speaker labels, and translation. Whisper made high-quality open STT universal; API services compete on latency and domain accuracy (medical, call-center). Word-error-rate on your own audio is the only benchmark that matters.

models.name: AssemblyAI Universal-2
models.note: API with speaker labels built in

best_pick: Whisper for open/self-hosted; Deepgram for streaming.
example_use: Live captions for a meeting.

demo.code:
from transformers import pipeline
asr = pipeline("automatic-speech-recognition", model="openai/whisper-large-v3")
print(asr("meeting.wav", return_timestamps=True)["text"][:200])

t: Text-to-speech — models that talk
title: Text-to-speech — models that talk
description: TTS synthesizes natural speech from text. The axes are naturalness, voice cloning from short samples, multilingual coverage, latency (streaming vs. batch), and whether it runs locally. Consent-gated cloning is the responsible norm for custom voices.
best_pick: ElevenLabs for quality; Piper for local/private.
example_use: Narrating an audiobook chapter.

demo.code:

client = ElevenLabs(api_key="EL_KEY")
audio = client.text_to_speech.convert(voice_id="narrator", model_id="eleven_v3",
    text="Chapter one. The archive was quiet.")
with open("ch1.mp3", "wb") as f:
    f.write(b"".join(audio))

t: Voice cloning — models that copy a voice
title: Voice cloning — models that copy a voice
description: Voice cloning reproduces a specific person's voice from a short sample, then speaks arbitrary text in it. Quality is now near-indistinguishable; the responsible practice is explicit consent from the voice owner plus watermarking or disclosure. Open options (XTTS v2, RVC) run locally.
best_pick: ElevenLabs for production; XTTS v2 for open/local.
example_use: A consenting narrator's voice for a whole series.

demo.code:
# XTTS v2 (open, local) cloning pattern:
from TTS.api import TTS
tts = TTS("tts_models/multilingual/multi-dataset/xtts_v2", gpu=True)
tts.tts_to_file("Hello, this is my cloned voice.", speaker_wav="consent_sample.wav",
                language="en", file_path="out.wav")
# Only clone voices you own or have written consent for.
demo.notes: Real Coqui TTS pattern with the consent rule stated.

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Speaker diarization — models that separate speakers
title: Speaker diarization — models that separate speakers
description: Diarization answers 'who spoke when' — splitting audio into speaker turns. It powers meeting transcripts with names attached, call analytics, and subtitle attribution. pyannote's open pipeline is the research standard; APIs bundle it with transcription.
best_pick: pyannote for open pipelines; AssemblyAI for one-call.
example_use: A board meeting transcript with speaker names.

demo.code:
from pyannote.audio import Pipeline
pipe = Pipeline.from_pretrained("pyannote/speaker-diarization-3.1")
for turn, _, spk in pipe("board.mp3").itertracks(yield_label=True):
    print(f"{turn.start:.1f}-{turn.end:.1f}s {spk}")
demo.notes: Real pyannote pattern (needs HF token for gated models).

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.

t: Music generation — models that compose
title: Music generation — models that compose
description: Music models compose full tracks from text prompts — melody, arrangement, and sometimes vocals. Suno/Udio lead as services; open models (MusicGen, Stable Audio Open) let you generate locally. Licensing of training data and outputs remains the live legal question in this space.

music = pipeline("text-to-audio", model="facebook/musicgen-small")
audio = music("upbeat folk tune, acoustic guitar", forward_params={"do_sample": True})

title: Audio understanding — models that listen deeply

t: Text embeddings — models that vectorize meaning
title: Text embeddings — models that vectorize meaning
description: Embeddings turn text into vectors so similarity becomes math — the foundation of semantic search and RAG retrieval. Multilingual models, long-context embeddings, and matched query/document encoders are the quality levers. Open models (BGE, E5) rival APIs for many workloads.
best_pick: Embed v3 multilingual; BGE-M3/E5 when it must be open.
example_use: Semantic search over a knowledge base.

demo.code:
from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
model = SentenceTransformer("BAAI/bge-m3")
vecs = model.encode(["refund policy text..."], normalize_embeddings=True)
print(vecs.shape)  # cosine-search these against embedded queries

t: Reranking — models that re-order search results
title: Reranking — models that re-order search results
description: Rerankers take the top-N results from fast vector search and re-score them precisely — the cheap trick that lifts RAG accuracy more than any other single change. Cross-encoder rerankers read query+document together instead of comparing vectors.
best_pick: Cohere Rerank API; bge-reranker for open stacks.
example_use: Reordering 50 candidates down to the best 5 for RAG.

demo.code:
import cohere
co = cohere.Client("COHERE_KEY")
r = co.rerank(model="rerank-english-v3.0", query="refund window?",
              documents=["30-day refunds...", "Shipping takes..."], top_n=1)
print(r.results[0].index, r.results[0].relevance_score)

t: RAG pipelines — models that answer from your documents
title: RAG pipelines — models that answer from your documents
description: Retrieval-augmented generation grounds answers in your own documents: retrieve chunks, stuff them into context, generate with citations. The model-side needs are long context, citation behavior, and honesty about missing info. Frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack) orchestrate; these models answer.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.note: Open RAG reader for private corpora

best_pick: Command R+ for cited enterprise RAG.
example_use: A support bot answering strictly from the help center.

co = cohere.Client("COHERE_KEY")
resp = co.chat(model="command-r-plus-08-2024", message="How do I reset my password?",
    documents=[{"title": "Help", "snippet": "Settings > Security > Reset password."}],
    citation_quality="accurate")
print(resp.text)
print(resp.citations)

t: Function calling / tool use — models that act
title: Function calling / tool use — models that act
description: Tool use lets models call your functions — search, databases, APIs — mid-conversation, turning chat into software. The capability to check: schema adherence (valid JSON args), parallel calls, and knowing when NOT to call. This is the foundation every agent is built on.
best_pick: GPT-4o/Claude for reliability; Hermes 3 open.
example_use: A travel bot that actually checks live prices.

demo.code:
from openai import OpenAI
import json
client = OpenAI()
tools = [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "get_price",
    "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"route": {"type": "string"}}}}}]
r = client.chat.completions.create(model="gpt-4o",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "Price NYC to Boston Friday"}], tools=tools)
print(r.choices[0].message.tool_calls[0].function.arguments)
demo.notes: Real function-calling pattern; execute the call yourself, then reply.

provenance: Public model cards, provider documentation, and open model repository metadata.
